transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 75 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sasha Irwin (Redwood SE), Marcus Ng (Riverbend CTO), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Priya Shah (Infra), Tim O'Leary (Product)

Summary:
Brief workshop to map Riverbend's latency (p95) and throughput targets to possible Redwood deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), decide scope for a pilot, and align on benchmark plan and success metrics. Heavy focus on streaming chat latency, cold-start p95, and concurrency token/s throughput.

Topics:
- Current infra and model stack (Lena)
- Target SLOs: p95 < 150ms for short assistant replies, 95th p95 for streaming? (discussion)
- Concurrency and burst profile (timing of peaks)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs: isolation, cost predictability, VPC/private requirements
- Benchmark plan and next steps

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jenna (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll do 60 to 75, want to focus on the p95 targets and what that means for hosting vs dedicated or private deploys
[00:12] Marcus (Riverbend): yeah thanks, we got a lot riding on this. Our clinical assistant needs tight latency for triage flows, around 100-150ms p95 for short replies, and streaming token throughput of ~1.2k tokens/sec during peak patient sessions
[00:28] Marco (Redwood SE): ok so couple clarifying q's: when you say 1.2k tokens/sec is that aggregate across all users or per-conversation burst?
[00:35] Lena (ML): it's aggregate during peak windows, but per-convo peaks are around 250 tokens/sec for power users. We have about 180 concurrent active sessions at busiest times, but only 30 persistent streaming sessions typically
[00:50] Priya (Infra): our concern is cold-starts — if a new shard wakes up we can't have 2s+ p95 on initial tokens, we need graceful degradation. Also our security team will push for VPC peering and customer-managed keys
[01:06] Sasha (Redwood SE): noted. For cold starts we advise keeping warmed pools or use dedicated capacity with burst slots. Redwood Dedicate — sorry Redwood Dedicated — lets you reserve GPUs with predictable warm-cache behaviour, which helps steady p95; hosted can work too but you'd see more variance without warm standby
[01:28] Tim (Product): cost is a factor; if Dedicated means reserve a bunch of GPUs we need clear unit-economics vs hosted pay-as-you-go. Do you have a model for token cost at different concurrency bands?
[01:40] Jenna: yes we'll share a detailed sheet, but rough rule: at low concurrency hosted with smart batching beats reserved if utilization low; once you hit steady concurrent streams (like your 30 persistent) Dedicated becomes more cost effective and consistent for p95
[01:55] Marcus: what about quantization? We plan to run a 13B param open model QA variant with q4 and maybe int8. How does that affect p95 and token/sec?
[02:06] Marco: quantization reduces memory and can speed up throughput but depends on kernels. For streaming and low-latency we tune the compilation and kernel selection; some quant paths slightly increase per-token latency but overall throughput maybe 20-40% better. We have internal benchmarks, will run with your exact model and sample prompts
[02:25] [crosstalk] Lena: also KV cache behaviour is crucial for us — we reuse context heavily across turns
[02:31] Marco: yep our runtime keeps KV cache hot for active sessions; for dedicated you can pin sessions to a pool so cache hit rate stays high, which reduces p95 for repeated-turn flows
[02:44] Priya: network overhead — how much does VPC peering add? Our infra team estimates ~20-30ms on average for cross-region peering
[02:52] Sasha: VPC adds a small fixed tail, yes; we can mitigate with regional routing and edge egress configs. For on-prem/private installs you avoid peering overhead but you take on ops burden
[03:07] Marcus: ok metrics — we want: p95 streaming first token < 120ms, steady-state per-token p95 < 80ms, and bulk throughput target of 1.2k tokens/sec sustained for 5min windows. Is that realistic?
[03:22] Marco: those are aggressive but feasible with Dedicated + warmed pools and optimized kernels on A100/H100 class GPUs. For Hosted it depends on overall load on the shared fleet, but we can give SLO-backed Dedicated options
[03:35] Jenna: also important to call out fallback policies — if Dedicated saturated we route to a compatible lower-cost variant or queued short responses to keep latency SLOs on essential paths
[03:47] Tim: do you have multi-region failover for latency-sensitive routing?
[03:51] Sasha: yes, smart routing can prefer region-local pools and failover to nearby regions; we can surface per-request latency policies in the API so you can pick regional pins
[04:05] Marcus: can we run a short benchmark with our prompts? We can supply 10k prompts including streaming chat transcripts
[04:10] Marco: absolutely. We'll need sample traces (timestamps, token counts) and a small infra key to hit the benchmark runner. Prefer to run both hosted throttled and dedicated so you can compare p95 and cost per token
[04:23] [30s pause — file sharing]
[04:54] Jenna: i'll share two artifacts after the call: 1) pricing/pilot deck, 2) benchmark template + infra checklist link (https://drive.re/redwood/rb-bench-2026). Also SOC2/ISO and network diagram
[05:07] Lena: one more constraint — our privacy team requires customer-managed KMS for key material; is that supported in hosted?
[05:13] Sasha: hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in our higher tiers; for full control you can run Private (VPC/on-prem) where keys never leave your cloud account
[05:25] Marcus: we might start with Hosted Dedicated to move quickly then shift to Private for compliance if pilot goes well
[05:32] Tim: how long to spin up a Dedicated pool for pilot?
[05:35] Marco: for pilot we can provision a small dedicated pool in 48-72 hours assuming quota; for full-scale you'll need lead time depending on GPU availability
[05:45] Priya: curious about KV cache warm strategies — if users are infrequent, how do you avoid cold cache thrash?
[05:52] Marco: we use TTLs and LRU heuristics, plus prefetched prefixes for known flows. For Dedicated you can give us sample session ids to pin. There's also a hybrid: keep small warm pool for tail flows
[06:05] Marcus: competitors — we've tried a triton-based local runner but struggled with scaling orchestration; also looked at Anthropic's hosted offering but their streaming had higher p95 in our tests
[06:16] Jenna: noted. We'll include benchmark comparatives where available but run your own samples is best
[06:22] Tim: whats the monitoring surface? we need per-request token latency, trace ids, and retention for 90 days
[06:28] Sasha: Console gives per-route latency, token breakdown, and trace hooks; we can ship extended retention as an add-on. Audit logs and SSO/SAML are supported for Enterprise accounts
[06:40] [minor transcription glitch - "KV cache" recorded as "K V case"]
[06:46] Marco: one technical note — streaming p95 is tricky because network jitter and buffering affect the first-byte; we measure both first-byte and full-turn p95 and recommend SLOs per metric
[06:58] Marcus: ok that helps. Pilot success criteria: meet p95 targets for 95% of test prompts, demonstrate sustained 1.2k tokens/sec for 5min, and confirm KMS + VPC peering works end-to-end
[07:12] Jenna: agreed. i'll follow up with the pricing/pilot deck and a proposed runbook. schedule follow-up May 19 to review results.
[07:20] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone
[07:25] [end meeting]
